verse.text: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other.

devotional.title: Joy in Both Seasons
devotional.body: Prosperity teaches us to rejoice, and adversity teaches us to think deeply. God uses both seasons to shape our character. Enjoy the good days fully, and let the hard days grow you rather than break you.
devotional.reflection: What is the current season teaching you about God and about yourself?
devotional.prayer: Lord, help me rejoice in good days and learn in hard ones. Amen.

verse.text: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.

devotional.title: The Whole Duty
devotional.body: After examining everything life has to offer, the Preacher lands on one conclusion: fear God and keep His commandments. Everything else is commentary. At the end of your life, this is what will still matter.
devotional.reflection: If this is the whole duty of man, how is your life measuring up?
devotional.prayer: Lord, help me to fear You and keep Your commandments with my whole life. Amen.

verse.text: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.

devotional.title: His Banner of Love
devotional.body: The image is a striking one: a banner lifted over you that declares love. God's love is not hidden or private; it is a banner raised for all to see. You are covered by a love that claims you openly.
devotional.reflection: How does it change you to know that love is the banner over your life?
devotional.prayer: Lord, thank You that Your banner over me is love. Let me live under it boldly. Amen.

verse.text: Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid: for the Lord Jehovah is my strength and my song.

devotional.title: Trust and Not Be Afraid
devotional.body: Isaiah made a decision of the will: God is my salvation, so I will trust and not be afraid. Fear is a natural feeling, but trusting God is a deliberate choice. Make that choice before the fear arrives.
devotional.reflection: What fear can you replace with a deliberate choice to trust today?
devotional.prayer: Lord, You are my salvation and my strength. I will trust You and not be afraid. Amen.

verse.text: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.

devotional.title: Perfect Peace
devotional.body: Perfect peace is promised to the one whose mind is fixed on God. Your peace level often matches the object of your thoughts. When your mind wanders to worry, bring it back to Him and peace returns.
devotional.reflection: What has your mind been fixed on that is stealing your peace?
devotional.prayer: Lord, keep my mind stayed on You so that I may have Your perfect peace. Amen.

verse.text: Trust ye in the Lord for ever: for in the Lord Jehovah is everlasting strength.

devotional.title: Everlasting Strength
devotional.body: Human strength runs out, but the Lord holds everlasting strength. That is why the call is to trust Him forever, not just in crisis. Your confidence should not be in your own endurance but in His.
devotional.reflection: Where are you leaning on your own strength instead of His everlasting one?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I trust in You forever, for in You is everlasting strength. Amen.

verse.text: And therefore will the Lord wait, that he may be gracious unto you.

devotional.title: He Waits to Be Gracious
devotional.body: God is not slow to bless you reluctantly; He waits eagerly to be gracious. His seeming delay is not neglect but grace preparing. He is not holding back from you; He is working toward your good.
devotional.reflection: How does it change your view of waiting to know God is waiting to be gracious to you?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I trust that You are waiting to be gracious to me. Teach me to wait on You. Amen.

verse.text: The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever.

devotional.title: His Word Stands Forever
devotional.body: Everything around you is temporary, like grass and flowers that wither. But the word of God stands forever. When everything else fades, one thing remains. Build your life on the thing that cannot fade.
devotional.reflection: What are you building on that will not last?
devotional.prayer: Lord, anchor my life on Your word, which stands forever. Amen.

verse.text: He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.

devotional.title: Power to the Faint
devotional.body: God does not give strength only to the strong; He gives power to the faint and increases strength in those who have none. Your weakness is not a disqualification; it is an invitation for His power.
devotional.reflection: In what area of weakness do you need to receive God's power today?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I am faint. Give me Your power and increase my strength. Amen.

verse.text: But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.

devotional.title: Renewed Strength
devotional.body: The promise is that waiting on the Lord renews strength. It sounds backwards, but it is true: rest in God produces the energy to run. Do not push through in your own strength; wait, and let Him renew you.
devotional.reflection: Are you waiting on the Lord or running ahead in your own energy?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I wait on You. Renew my strength and lift me up like the wings of an eagle. Amen.

verse.text: For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee.

devotional.title: I Will Help You
devotional.body: There is intimacy in God holding your right hand, like a parent steadying a child taking uncertain steps. He speaks the same words to you: Fear not; I will help you. You do not walk alone.
devotional.reflection: Where do you need to feel God's hand steadying you today?
devotional.prayer: Lord, hold my right hand and help me not to fear. I trust You to steady my steps. Amen.

verse.text: When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee.

devotional.title: Through the Waters
devotional.body: Notice the promise is not that you will avoid the waters but that you will pass through them without being overwhelmed. God does not always remove the flood; He goes with you into it. His presence is the difference.
devotional.reflection: What waters are you passing through that God is walking with you in?
devotional.prayer: Lord, be with me in the waters and keep them from overflowing me. Amen.

verse.text: Behold, I will do a new thing; now it shall spring forth; shall ye not know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.

devotional.title: A New Thing
devotional.body: God is not confined to your history or your wilderness. He makes ways where there are none and rivers in deserts. Do not assume that because it has not happened yet, God cannot do it. Watch for the new thing He is doing.
devotional.reflection: What new thing might God be doing in a part of your life that feels dry?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I look for the new thing You are doing. Make a way in my wilderness. Amen.

verse.text: And even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you.

devotional.title: Carried to the End
devotional.body: God's care is not for the early years only. He carries you even to old age, all the way to the end. You will never reach a season where He drops you. His faithfulness spans your entire life.
devotional.reflection: How does God's promise to carry you to the end change how you face aging?
devotional.prayer: Lord, carry me through every season of my life, even to the end. Amen.

verse.text: Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands.

devotional.title: Graven on His Hands
devotional.body: God says your name is carved into the palms of His hands, a permanent reminder that He will never forget you. When you wonder if anyone remembers you, remember this: the Creator of the universe has engraved you on His own hands.
devotional.reflection: What makes you doubt that God remembers and cares for you?
devotional.prayer: Lord, thank You that You have graven me on the palms of Your hands. I am never forgotten. Amen.

verse.text: But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.

devotional.title: Healed by His Stripes
devotional.body: This verse points to the heart of the gospel: Jesus took the wounds our sin deserved so that we could have peace and healing. The punishment that should have fallen on us fell on Him. Receive the peace He purchased.
devotional.reflection: Have you truly accepted the peace that Jesus purchased with His wounds?
devotional.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for being wounded for me. I receive Your peace and healing. Amen.

verse.text: For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the Lord. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.

devotional.title: Higher Ways
devotional.body: God's thoughts and ways are higher than yours, as far as the heavens are above the earth. This means some things will not make sense to you yet. It is not a reason to stop trusting but a reason to trust more.
devotional.reflection: What is God doing that you do not understand but can trust Him with?
devotional.prayer: Lord, Your ways are higher than mine. I trust Your wisdom above my understanding. Amen.

verse.text: So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please.

devotional.title: His Word Never Returns Empty
devotional.body: God's word always accomplishes what He sends it to do. It does not fail, drift, or return without effect. When God speaks over your life, His word is working, even when you cannot see it yet.
devotional.reflection: What has God spoken that you need to trust is still at work?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I trust that Your word is at work in my life and will not return empty. Amen.

verse.text: And the Lord shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought.

devotional.title: Guide Continually
devotional.body: God promises to guide you continually and to satisfy your soul even in dry seasons. His guidance is not occasional but constant. Even in your drought, He has a way to satisfy your soul.
devotional.reflection: Where do you need God's guidance, and where does your soul feel dry?
devotional.prayer: Lord, guide me continually and satisfy my soul even in this dry season. Amen.

verse.text: Blessed is the man that trusteth in the Lord, and whose hope the Lord is.

devotional.title: Blessed Is the Trusting
devotional.body: Blessing is attached not to circumstances but to trust. The person who trusts in the Lord and makes the Lord their hope is blessed regardless of what happens around them. Your hope has a name.
devotional.reflection: Is your hope in the Lord or in outcomes you cannot control?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I make You my hope. Bless me as I trust in You. Amen.

verse.text: Heal me, O Lord, and I shall be healed; save me, and I shall be saved: for thou art my praise.

devotional.title: Heal Me, O Lord
devotional.body: Jeremiah prayed with complete dependence: if the Lord heals, healing happens; if the Lord saves, salvation comes. All healing ultimately traces back to His hand. Bring your whole self to the Great Physician.
devotional.reflection: What in your life needs the healing that only the Lord can bring?
devotional.prayer: Lord, heal me and I shall be healed. Save me and I shall be saved. You are my praise. Amen.

verse.text: And ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart.

devotional.title: Found When You Search
devotional.body: God promises to be found by those who search for Him with their whole heart. He is not playing hide and seek; He wants to be found. The condition is not perfection but sincerity of heart.
devotional.reflection: Are you seeking God with your whole heart or half-heartedly?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I search for You with all my heart. Let me find You today. Amen.

verse.text: Behold, I am the Lord, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?

devotional.title: Nothing Too Hard
devotional.body: God asks a question that settles every fear: is anything too hard for Him? The answer is no. Whatever seems impossible to you is not impossible to the God of all flesh.
devotional.reflection: What have you labeled as impossible that God is asking you to bring to Him?
devotional.prayer: Lord, nothing is too hard for You. I bring my impossibilities to Your power. Amen.

verse.text: Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not.

devotional.title: Call and I Will Answer
devotional.body: God invites you to call on Him and promises to answer, showing you great and hidden things you do not yet know. Some things are only revealed through prayer. Call on Him and expect revelation.
devotional.reflection: What are you asking God to show you that you do not yet know?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I call on You. Answer me and show me great and mighty things. Amen.

verse.text: Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.

devotional.title: Turn Again to the Lord
devotional.body: In the middle of lament, Jeremiah called for honest self-examination and a return to God. Growth requires looking inward and then turning upward. Examine your ways, and where you have drifted, come back.
devotional.reflection: Where have you drifted, and what step of return is God asking of you?
devotional.prayer: Lord, search my ways and lead me back to You when I have wandered. Amen.

verse.text: The Lord is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him.

devotional.title: Good to Those Who Wait
devotional.body: Written in the ruins of Jerusalem, this verse declares that the Lord is good to those who wait for Him. Even in devastation, God's goodness does not stop for those who seek Him. Hold on to that hope.
devotional.reflection: How can you keep seeking God's goodness while you are still waiting?
devotional.prayer: Lord, You are good to those who wait for You. Help me keep seeking Your goodness. Amen.

verse.text: I will seek that which was lost, and bring again that which was driven away.

devotional.title: He Seeks the Lost
devotional.body: God does not wait for the lost to find their way back; He goes to seek them. If you feel lost, scattered, or far from home, know that the Shepherd is searching for you. His love moves toward you.
devotional.reflection: Where do you feel lost, and are you willing to let the Shepherd find you?
devotional.prayer: Lord, seek me where I am lost and bring me back. I trust Your love to find me. Amen.

verse.text: A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you.

devotional.title: A New Heart
devotional.body: God's promise goes beyond behavior modification; He offers a new heart and a new spirit. He does not just want you to try harder; He wants to change you from the inside. Receive the heart He offers.
devotional.reflection: What do you need God to change from the inside rather than just on the surface?
devotional.prayer: Lord, give me a new heart and put a new spirit within me. Change me from the inside. Amen.

verse.text: And he changeth the times and the seasons: he removeth kings, and setteth up kings: he giveth wisdom unto the wise, and knowledge to them that know understanding.

devotional.title: God Is in Control
devotional.body: Daniel understood that leaders rise and fall at God's command and that times and seasons change under His hand. Nothing in the news surprises Him. Your circumstances are not random; they are under His sovereign care.
devotional.reflection: How does knowing God is sovereign over rulers and seasons calm your heart?
devotional.prayer: Lord, You are in control of all things. Help me trust Your sovereignty today. Amen.

verse.text: For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.

devotional.title: Mercy Over Sacrifice
devotional.body: God cares more about the condition of your heart than the size of your offerings. Religious activity can never replace a life of mercy and a genuine knowledge of God. He wants your heart more than your performance.
devotional.reflection: Are you offering God religious activity while withholding your heart?
devotional.prayer: Lord, give me a heart of mercy and a true knowledge of You, not just outward religion. Amen.

verse.text: I will heal their backsliding, I will love them freely.

devotional.title: Healed and Loved Freely
devotional.body: Even when God's people wandered, He promised to heal their backsliding and love them freely. God's love does not have to be earned and is not withdrawn when you stumble. His love is the reason you can come home.
devotional.reflection: What wandering do you need God's healing love to restore?
devotional.prayer: Lord, heal my backsliding and love me freely. Bring me back to You. Amen.

verse.text: And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the Lord your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness.

devotional.title: Rend Your Heart
devotional.body: The call was to tear the heart, not just the clothes, in repentance. Outward displays mean little if the heart is unchanged. God is gracious and merciful, so you can turn to Him honestly and find forgiveness.
devotional.reflection: Is your repentance changing your heart or just your appearance?
devotional.prayer: Lord, tear my heart and turn me to You. I trust Your grace and mercy. Amen.

verse.text: But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.

devotional.title: Let Righteousness Flow
devotional.body: God is not impressed by worship that ignores justice and righteousness. His desire is that fairness and right living flow through society like a powerful stream. Your faith should produce fruit in how you treat others.
devotional.reflection: Where is God calling you to stand for justice and live righteously?
devotional.prayer: Lord, let justice and righteousness flow through my life like a mighty stream. Amen.

verse.text: He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the Lord require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?

devotional.title: Do Justly, Love Mercy
devotional.body: God has already told you what is good: act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with Him. This is not complicated, but it is demanding. It is a lifestyle, not a checklist.
devotional.reflection: Which of the three are you weakest in: justice, mercy, or humility?
devotional.prayer: Lord, help me do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with You every day. Amen.

verse.text: The Lord is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.

devotional.title: A Strong Hold
devotional.body: Nahum wrote about judgment, but he also wrote about refuge. The Lord is good, a strong hold in trouble, and He knows those who trust in Him. In a world of instability, He is your secure place.
devotional.reflection: Where do you run when trouble comes, and does it include the Lord?
devotional.prayer: Lord, You are my strong hold in the day of trouble. I trust in You. Amen.

verse.text: For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea.

devotional.title: Glory Fills the Earth
devotional.body: One day the knowledge of God's glory will cover the earth like the waters cover the sea. That is the direction history is moving. Even when the present looks dark, this promise gives unshakable hope.
devotional.reflection: How does the promise of God's glory filling the earth anchor your hope today?
devotional.prayer: Lord, let the knowledge of Your glory grow in me and fill the earth. Amen.

verse.text: The Lord God is my strength, and he will make my feet like hinds' feet, and he will make me to walk upon mine high places.

devotional.title: Feet Like the Deer
devotional.body: The deer is sure-footed on steep, rocky ground, and God promises to give you that same stability on the high places of life. Your strength is not in the terrain but in the Lord who trains your feet.
devotional.reflection: What high, hard place do you need God to steady your feet on?
devotional.prayer: Lord, be my strength and make my feet sure on the high places. Amen.

verse.text: The Lord thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love.

devotional.title: He Rejoices Over You
devotional.body: This is one of the most tender pictures of God in the Bible. He is mighty to save, and He rejoices over you with joy and rests in His love for you. God does not merely tolerate you; He delights in you.
devotional.reflection: How does knowing God rejoices over you change how you see yourself?
devotional.prayer: Lord, thank You that You rejoice over me with joy. Let me rest in Your love. Amen.

verse.text: Yet now be strong, O Zerubbabel, saith the Lord; and be strong, O Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest; and be strong, all ye people of the land, saith the Lord, and work: for I am with you, saith the Lord of hosts.

devotional.title: Be Strong, I Am With You
devotional.body: God told His people to be strong and to work, and He gave them the reason: I am with you. Rebuilding was daunting, but the presence of God made it possible. Face your rebuilding with the same confidence.
devotional.reflection: What needs rebuilding in your life, and how does God's presence strengthen you?
devotional.prayer: Lord, make me strong to work, for You are with me. Amen.

verse.text: Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.

devotional.title: By My Spirit
devotional.body: The temple would not be rebuilt by military might or human strength but by the Spirit of God. What is impossible for you is possible when God's Spirit is at work. Learn to rely on Him rather than your own resources.
devotional.reflection: Where are you trusting human might when you need the Spirit of God?
devotional.prayer: Lord, do Your work in me by Your Spirit, not by my own power. Amen.

verse.text: For who hath despised the day of small things?

devotional.title: The Day of Small Things
devotional.body: It is easy to look down on small beginnings, but God honors them. Big works of God often start as small seeds. Do not despise the small step, the small obedience, or the small beginning. God is in the small things.
devotional.reflection: What small beginning has God placed in your hands that you have overlooked?
devotional.prayer: Lord, help me honor the small things and trust You to grow them. Amen.

verse.text: Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the Lord of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven.

devotional.title: Prove Me
devotional.body: God issues a rare challenge: test Him in giving and see if He will not open the windows of heaven. He is not afraid of being put to the test when it comes to His faithfulness. Give generously and trust His promise.
devotional.reflection: Are you willing to trust God's promise to bless generous giving?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I trust Your promise. Help me give faithfully and watch You provide. Amen.

verse.text: Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another: and the Lord hearkened, and heard it.

devotional.title: He Listens to Our Words
devotional.body: When God's people spoke to one another about Him, the Lord heard and listened. There is a book of remembrance for those who honor God in their conversation. Speak of God's goodness, and know He is listening.
devotional.reflection: What are you speaking about most often, and would God delight to hear it?
devotional.prayer: Lord, let my conversation honor You and bring encouragement to others. Amen.

verse.text: But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.

devotional.title: More Than Bread
devotional.body: When Jesus was tempted, He quoted this truth: life is sustained by more than food. Your deepest needs are fed by the Word of God. Physical provision matters, but spiritual nourishment matters more.
devotional.reflection: What is your soul feeding on, and is it enough?
devotional.prayer: Lord, feed my soul on Your word, which sustains me beyond bread. Amen.

verse.text: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.

devotional.title: Blessed Are Those Who Mourn
devotional.body: Jesus turns our understanding upside down by calling mourners blessed. God draws near to those who grieve, and His comfort is promised to them. Your mourning is not wasted; it is the doorway to His comfort.
devotional.reflection: What grief are you carrying that you can bring to the God of all comfort?
devotional.prayer: Lord, comfort me in my mourning. Let Your presence reach my sorrow. Amen.

verse.text: Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.

devotional.title: Hunger for Righteousness
devotional.body: Jesus promises satisfaction to those who hunger and thirst for righteousness. Like physical hunger, this longing drives you to God. Feed the hunger by seeking Him, and He promises you will be filled.
devotional.reflection: What are you hungering for, and is righteousness among your cravings?
devotional.prayer: Lord, create in me a hunger for righteousness that only You can satisfy. Amen.

verse.text: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.

devotional.title: Blessed Peacemakers
devotional.body: Jesus blesses not the peacekeepers who avoid conflict but the peacemakers who actively build peace. Making peace takes courage, wisdom, and humility. It is a family trait of God's children.
devotional.reflection: Where is God calling you to make peace rather than avoid it?
devotional.prayer: Lord, make me a peacemaker who reflects Your family in the world. Amen.

verse.text: Ye are the light of the world.

devotional.title: The Light of the World
devotional.body: Jesus did not say you should become light; He said you are light. You carry His light into dark places simply by being where He has placed you. Do not hide it; let it shine where you live and work.
devotional.reflection: What dark place around you is waiting for your light to be seen?
devotional.prayer: Lord, let me live as the light You have made me to be. Amen.

verse.text: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.

devotional.title: Let Your Light Shine
devotional.body: Your good works are not for your own glory but for the Father's. When people see your life, they should be drawn to God, not to you. Live visibly for Him, and let every good deed point upward.
devotional.reflection: Do your good works point people to God or to yourself?
devotional.prayer: Lord, let my life shine so that others may glorify You. Amen.

verse.text: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret.

devotional.title: Pray in Secret
devotional.body: Jesus taught that prayer does not need an audience. The Father sees what is done in secret and rewards openly. Your most powerful moments of prayer may be the ones no one else ever knows about.
devotional.reflection: Do you have a regular secret place where you meet God alone?
devotional.prayer: Lord, meet me in the secret place. Let my private prayers shape my public life. Amen.

verse.text: For your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.

devotional.title: He Knows Your Needs
devotional.body: God knows what you need before you ask. That does not make prayer pointless; it makes it relational. Prayer is not informing God of news He missed but drawing near to the Father who already knows and cares.
devotional.reflection: How does knowing God already knows your needs change the way you pray?
devotional.prayer: Lord, thank You that You know my needs before I ask. Teach me to pray from relationship. Amen.

verse.text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

devotional.title: Where Your Treasure Is
devotional.body: Your heart follows whatever you value most. If your treasure is in things that pass away, your heart will drift with them. Invest in what lasts, and you will find your heart anchored there.
devotional.reflection: Where is your treasure, and where has your heart followed?
devotional.prayer: Lord, help me invest in what lasts, so my heart stays with You. Amen.

verse.text: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?

devotional.title: Your Father Feeds Them
devotional.body: Jesus pointed to birds that do not worry about food, yet the heavenly Father feeds them. If He cares for them, how much more will He care for you? Worry is a sign you have forgotten the size of your Father.
devotional.reflection: What worry today contradicts the truth that your Father provides?
devotional.prayer: Father, if You feed the birds, I trust You to care for me. Calm my worry. Amen.

verse.text: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.

devotional.title: Do Not Worry About Tomorrow
devotional.body: Jesus tells you not to take on tomorrow's worries today. Each day has enough of its own concerns, and God's grace is given for today. Trust Him with tomorrow when it arrives.
devotional.reflection: What tomorrow-sized worry are you carrying today that you can release?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I release tomorrow to You. Help me live faithfully in today. Amen.

verse.text: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.

devotional.title: Ask, Seek, Knock
devotional.body: Jesus encourages persistent prayer: ask, seek, knock. The verbs suggest continuing action, not a single attempt. Keep asking, keep seeking, keep knocking, because God welcomes your persistence.
devotional.reflection: What have you stopped asking, seeking, or knocking for that you need to take up again?
devotional.prayer: Lord, give me persistence in prayer. Help me ask, seek, and knock without giving up. Amen.

verse.text: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.

devotional.title: The Golden Rule
devotional.body: Jesus summarized how to treat others: do to them what you would want done to you. This simple rule transforms relationships when practiced daily. Treat others the way you hope to be treated.
devotional.reflection: Who would benefit from you applying the golden rule today?
devotional.prayer: Lord, help me treat others the way I would want to be treated. Amen.

verse.text: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.

devotional.title: Moved With Compassion
devotional.body: Jesus saw people not as a crowd but as scattered sheep needing a shepherd. His compassion moved Him to act. Let the same compassion shape how you see the people around you.
devotional.reflection: Who in your life looks like scattered sheep needing the love of a shepherd?
devotional.prayer: Lord, give me Your compassion for the people around me. Move my heart to help. Amen.

verse.text: Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.

devotional.title: Confess Him
devotional.body: Jesus connects our boldness to acknowledge Him with His willingness to acknowledge us before the Father. When you openly belong to Christ, He openly stands for you. Your confession matters.
devotional.reflection: In what situation have you been reluctant to acknowledge Christ openly?
devotional.prayer: Lord, give me courage to confess You before others, knowing You confess me before the Father. Amen.

verse.text: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.

devotional.title: Learn of Me
devotional.body: Jesus offers rest to those who learn from Him, for He is meek and lowly in heart. The rest He gives is not laziness but peace that comes from walking with Him. Learn His ways, and your soul will find rest.
devotional.reflection: What are you learning from Jesus that is bringing rest to your soul?
devotional.prayer: Lord Jesus, teach me Your ways. Let my soul find rest as I learn from You. Amen.

verse.text: For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.

devotional.title: Out of the Abundance of the Heart
devotional.body: Your words are a window into your heart. Whatever fills your heart will overflow through your mouth. If you want better words, begin by tending to what fills your heart.
devotional.reflection: What do your recent words reveal is filling your heart?
devotional.prayer: Lord, fill my heart with good things so my mouth speaks what is good. Amen.

verse.text: For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.

devotional.title: Family of God
devotional.body: Jesus redefined family: those who do the will of the Father are His brothers and sisters. Your relationship with God creates bonds deeper than blood. You belong to a family that will never end.
devotional.reflection: How does belonging to God's family change how you relate to other believers?
devotional.prayer: Lord, thank You for making me part of Your family. Help me live as a faithful sibling. Amen.

verse.text: But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.

devotional.title: Be Not Afraid
devotional.body: Walking on water, Jesus spoke to His frightened disciples: Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid. When the storm feels overwhelming, His presence is the cure for fear. He is in the storm with you.
devotional.reflection: What storm has made you afraid, and where do you need to hear His voice?
devotional.prayer: Lord, when I am afraid in the storm, remind me that You are near. Amen.

verse.text: Then said Jesus unto his disciples, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.

devotional.title: Take Up Your Cross
devotional.body: Following Jesus involves denying yourself and taking up a cross. It is a life of surrender, not self-promotion. The cross you carry is not easy, but it leads to life that the world cannot give.
devotional.reflection: What is God asking you to deny yourself in order to follow Him more closely?
devotional.prayer: Lord, teach me to deny myself, take up my cross, and follow You every day. Amen.

verse.text: And Jesus said unto them, Because of your unbelief: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you.

devotional.title: Faith as a Mustard Seed
devotional.body: Jesus said even tiny faith, the size of a mustard seed, can move mountains. The point is not the size of your faith but the object of it. A little faith in a great God is enough.
devotional.reflection: What mountain stands before you, and will you speak to it with even a seed of faith?
devotional.prayer: Lord, grow my faith. Help me trust You with the mountains in my life. Amen.

verse.text: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.

devotional.title: Where Two or Three Gather
devotional.body: Jesus promises His presence where believers gather in His name, even in the smallest gatherings. You do not need a large crowd to meet God. Even two or three are enough for His presence to dwell.
devotional.reflection: Who could you gather with in Jesus' name to experience His presence?
devotional.prayer: Lord, be in the midst of our gatherings, however small they are. Amen.

verse.text: But Jesus said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.

devotional.title: Come With Childlike Faith
devotional.body: Jesus welcomed children and held them up as examples of the kingdom. Childlike faith is trusting, humble, and uncomplicated. Come to God without trying to earn His favor, just as a child comes to a loving parent.
devotional.reflection: What is complicating your faith that a childlike trust could simplify?
devotional.prayer: Lord, give me a faith that is simple, trusting, and childlike. Let me come to You freely. Amen.

verse.text: But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.

devotional.title: All Things Possible
devotional.body: Jesus acknowledged the limits of human ability before pointing to God's limitless power. What is impossible with men is possible with God. Bring your impossible to the God for whom nothing is impossible.
devotional.reflection: What seems impossible to you that you can place in God's hands today?
devotional.prayer: Lord, with You all things are possible. I give You what seems impossible to me. Amen.

verse.text: And all things, whatsoever ye shall ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive.

devotional.title: Believing Prayer
devotional.body: Jesus ties receiving to believing in prayer. This is not a blank check for anything you desire; it is a promise for those whose faith is in God. Pray believing that God is who He says He is.
devotional.reflection: What are you praying for, and are you praying with belief?
devotional.prayer: Lord, strengthen my belief as I pray. Let my requests be made in faith. Amen.

verse.text: Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.

devotional.title: Love the Lord
devotional.body: The greatest command is to love God with everything you are: heart, soul, and mind. This is not a partial devotion but a total one. Love for God is meant to be the driving force of your whole life.
devotional.reflection: Which part of you, heart, soul, or mind, is holding back from loving God fully?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I want to love You with all my heart, soul, and mind. Take all of me. Amen.

verse.text: And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.

devotional.title: Humbled and Exalted
devotional.body: Jesus reverses the world's ladder: those who push themselves up will be brought down, and those who humble themselves will be lifted up. Do not fight for recognition. Let God do the exalting.
devotional.reflection: Where are you trying to exalt yourself that you need to trust God with?
devotional.prayer: Lord, keep me humble and let You be the one who lifts me up. Amen.

verse.text: Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.

devotional.title: Words That Never Pass
devotional.body: Everything you can see will one day pass away, but the words of Jesus will never pass away. The most permanent thing in the universe is the Word of God. Build your life on what will outlast everything.
devotional.reflection: Are you building on things that will pass away or on words that will last?
devotional.prayer: Lord, Your words will never pass away. Anchor my life on them. Amen.

verse.text: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.

devotional.title: Go and Make Disciples
devotional.body: The Great Commission sends every believer into the world to make disciples. This is not a task for a few but a calling for all. Wherever you go, you are sent to represent and share the kingdom.
devotional.reflection: Who in your world is God sending you to reach with His love?
devotional.prayer: Lord, use me to make disciples wherever I go. Give me love for those You send me to. Amen.

verse.text: As soon as Jesus heard the word that was spoken, he saith unto the ruler of the synagogue, Be not afraid, only believe.

devotional.title: Only Believe
devotional.body: When news came that the girl had died, Jesus told the father: Be not afraid, only believe. Bad news does not cancel God's ability. In the moments that feel final, keep believing.
devotional.reflection: What bad news are you letting silence your faith today?
devotional.prayer: Lord, when I hear hard news, help me not be afraid but only believe. Amen.

verse.text: Jesus said unto him, If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth.

devotional.title: Believe
devotional.body: A desperate father said, 'If thou canst do anything,' and Jesus turned the question back to him: If you can believe. The issue was not Jesus' ability but the man's belief. Let your faith be the question you ask God.
devotional.reflection: What are you doubting God can do that He is asking you to believe He can?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I believe; help my unbelief. Let all things be possible through faith in You. Amen.

verse.text: Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them.

devotional.title: Believe When You Pray
devotional.body: Jesus ties the outcome of prayer to faith. When you pray, believe that God has heard and that He will act. Faith is not pretending; it is trusting the One who has promised.
devotional.reflection: Do you pray with expectation, or do your words of prayer carry doubt?
devotional.prayer: Lord, when I pray, help me believe that You receive and answer. Amen.

verse.text: And when ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any.

devotional.title: Forgive When You Pray
devotional.body: Jesus connected effective prayer to a forgiving heart. Holding grudges blocks the flow of grace. Before you pray, release the offenses you are carrying, and let forgiveness clear the way.
devotional.reflection: Who do you need to forgive so your prayers are not hindered?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I forgive those who have wronged me. Cleanse my heart as I come to pray. Amen.

verse.text: For with God nothing shall be impossible.

devotional.title: Nothing Impossible
devotional.body: The angel spoke these words to Mary when the promise seemed impossible. God does not operate within human limits. Whatever seems impossible in your situation is within His power.
devotional.reflection: What are you treating as impossible that you need to submit to God's power?
devotional.prayer: Lord, with You nothing is impossible. I trust You with what seems impossible. Amen.

verse.text: And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people.

devotional.title: Good Tidings of Great Joy
devotional.body: The angels' announcement of Jesus' birth was a message of great joy for all people. God's love broke into a waiting world. Whatever the season, the news that God is with us is still the greatest joy available.
devotional.reflection: How can the good news of Jesus bring joy to your heart today?
devotional.prayer: Lord, thank You for the good tidings of great joy. Let Your coming fill my heart with joy. Amen.

verse.text: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom.

devotional.title: Give and It Shall Be Given
devotional.body: Jesus describes generosity with a picture of abundance: a measure pressed down, shaken together, and running over. Giving is not loss; it is the doorway to receiving. Open your hand, and watch God fill it.
devotional.reflection: What could you give today that might come back pressed down and running over?
devotional.prayer: Lord, make me generous. I trust that giving opens the way to Your abundance. Amen.

verse.text: And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?

devotional.title: Lord, Lord
devotional.body: Jesus challenged those who called Him Lord but did not obey Him. Words of devotion mean little without a life that follows. Let your 'Lord' be backed by your obedience.
devotional.reflection: Is there an area where you call Jesus Lord but are not obeying Him?
devotional.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are my Lord. Help me not only say it but live it. Amen.

verse.text: He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.

devotional.title: Built on the Rock
devotional.body: Jesus compared those who hear and obey His words to a man who dug deep and built on rock. The same storm tested both houses; the foundation made the difference. Build your life on obedience to Christ.
devotional.reflection: When storms come, what foundation is your life standing on?
devotional.prayer: Lord, help me dig deep and build my life on the rock of Your word. Amen.

verse.text: Wherefore I say unto thee, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much.

devotional.title: Forgiven Much, Loves Much
devotional.body: The woman who washed Jesus' feet loved much because she knew she had been forgiven much. Forgiveness produces love, and love produces devotion. Remember how much you have been forgiven, and your love will grow.
devotional.reflection: Does your love for Jesus match the forgiveness you have received?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I have been forgiven much. Let my love for You reflect that grace. Amen.

verse.text: And he said unto them, Where is your faith?

devotional.title: Where Is Your Faith?
devotional.body: In the middle of a terrifying storm, Jesus asked His disciples where their faith was. The storm was real, but their faith was missing. Faith does not remove storms; it keeps you from being mastered by them.
devotional.reflection: In your current storm, where has your faith gone?
devotional.prayer: Lord, help me find my faith in the middle of the storm. Amen.

verse.text: And he said, He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.

devotional.title: Go and Do Likewise
devotional.body: The Good Samaritan saw a stranger in need and stopped to help while others passed by. Jesus closed the story with a command: go and do likewise. Mercy is not a feeling; it is action.
devotional.reflection: Who in need have you been passing by that God is calling you to help?
devotional.prayer: Lord, make me a neighbor who shows mercy in action, not just in word. Amen.

verse.text: But he said, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.

devotional.title: Hear and Keep
devotional.body: Jesus blessed those who hear the Word of God and keep it. Hearing alone is not enough; keeping means living it out. The blessing comes when what you hear becomes how you live.
devotional.reflection: What have you heard from God recently that you have not yet put into practice?
devotional.prayer: Lord, make me not only a hearer but a keeper of Your word. Amen.

verse.text: But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.

devotional.title: Your Hairs Are Numbered
devotional.body: God's attention to detail extends to the hairs on your head. If He cares about such small details, you can trust Him with the big ones. You are of more value to Him than you can imagine.
devotional.reflection: What concern is convincing you that God does not care about the details?
devotional.prayer: Lord, thank You for caring about every detail of my life. I will not fear. Amen.

verse.text: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom.

devotional.title: Little Flock
devotional.body: Jesus calls His followers a little flock and reassures them that it is the Father's good pleasure to give them the kingdom. God delights to give. His good pleasure is your good gift.
devotional.reflection: How does knowing God delights to give you the kingdom quiet your fears?
devotional.prayer: Father, thank You for the good pleasure of giving me the kingdom. I will not fear. Amen.

verse.text: I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth.

devotional.title: Joy in Heaven
devotional.body: When one person turns back to God, heaven celebrates. Your repentance is not a burden God endures; it is a joy He shares. If heaven rejoices over you, you can be sure God receives you gladly.
devotional.reflection: Do you believe God rejoices over you when you return to Him?
devotional.prayer: Lord, thank You that heaven rejoices when I turn to You. Bring me close again. Amen.

verse.text: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.

devotional.title: Faithful in the Least
devotional.body: Jesus taught that faithfulness in small things proves you can be trusted with greater things. The little responsibilities you handle today are training for the larger ones tomorrow. Be faithful where you are.
devotional.reflection: What small responsibility has God entrusted to you that you have been neglecting?
devotional.prayer: Lord, make me faithful in the little things so I can be trusted with more. Amen.

verse.text: Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you.

devotional.title: The Kingdom Within
devotional.body: Jesus said the kingdom of God is within you. It is not only a future place but a present reality in your heart. When God rules within, His kingdom goes wherever you go.
devotional.reflection: Is the kingdom of God ruling within your heart today?
devotional.prayer: Lord, let Your kingdom reign within me and overflow through my life. Amen.

verse.text: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.

devotional.title: He Came to Seek
devotional.body: Jesus came not for those who had everything together but for the lost. No matter how far you have wandered, His mission is to seek and save you. You are never too lost for Him.
devotional.reflection: Where in your life do you need to let Jesus find you and save you?
devotional.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for coming to seek me. Save what is lost in me. Amen.

verse.text: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.

devotional.title: I Have Prayed for You
devotional.body: Jesus told Peter that He had prayed for him that his faith would not fail. Before Peter even faced his trial, Jesus was interceding for him. Jesus is praying for you too, even in your hardest moments.
devotional.reflection: How does knowing Jesus is praying for you change how you face your trials?
devotional.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for praying for me. Sustain my faith through every trial. Amen.

verse.text: He is not here, but is risen: remember how he spake unto you.

devotional.title: He Is Risen
devotional.body: The empty tomb is the foundation of Christian hope. Jesus is not here; He is risen. Every promise He made is backed by His resurrection power. Death could not hold Him, and nothing can hold His promises.
devotional.reflection: What hopeless situation is the reality of the resurrection challenging today?
devotional.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are risen! Let the power of Your resurrection meet my life today. Amen.

verse.text: And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.

devotional.title: Light in the Darkness
devotional.body: Jesus is the light that shines into darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it. No matter how deep the darkness around you, the light of Christ still shines. Stand near the light.
devotional.reflection: What darkness needs the light of Christ to reach into today?
devotional.prayer: Lord, let Your light shine into every dark place in my life. Amen.

verse.text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us.

devotional.title: The Word Made Flesh
devotional.body: God did not stay distant; the Word became flesh and lived among us. Jesus is God with skin on, close enough to touch and know. Your God is not far off but near, dwelling among His people.
devotional.reflection: How does knowing God came near change the way you approach Him?
devotional.prayer: Lord, thank You for dwelling among us. Draw near to me and let me know You. Amen.

verse.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

devotional.title: The Greatest Love
devotional.body: This verse holds the whole gospel in one sentence: God loved, God gave, and whoever believes lives forever. His love is not general; it reaches you personally. Believe, and receive everlasting life.
devotional.reflection: Have you personally received the gift this verse describes?
devotional.prayer: God, thank You for loving me enough to give Your Son. I believe in Jesus and receive everlasting life. Amen.

verse.text: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.

devotional.title: Living Water
devotional.body: Jesus offered the woman at the well a water that would quench her deepest thirst forever. Everything else you reach for leaves you thirsty again. Only Jesus satisfies the soul from within.
devotional.reflection: What have you been drinking from that never truly satisfies?
devotional.prayer: Lord, give me Your living water. Satisfy the thirst only You can quench. Amen.

verse.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.

devotional.title: Everlasting Life Now
devotional.body: Jesus said eternal life is not only a future hope but a present possession. Those who hear and believe have already passed from death to life. Your eternity is settled, so live today with confidence.
devotional.reflection: How does knowing you already have everlasting life change how you live today?
devotional.prayer: Lord, thank You that I have passed from death to life. Let that truth shape my day. Amen.

verse.text: And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.

devotional.title: The Bread of Life
devotional.body: Jesus called Himself the bread of life, the sustenance the soul truly needs. Just as bread feeds the body daily, coming to Jesus feeds the soul. Come to Him, and your deeper hungers will be met.
devotional.reflection: What are you feeding your soul that leaves it hungry for something more?
devotional.prayer: Jesus, You are the bread of life. Feed my soul and satisfy my deepest hunger. Amen.

verse.text: He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.

devotional.title: Rivers of Living Water
devotional.body: Faith in Jesus does not just fill you; it overflows. The Spirit within you becomes rivers of living water that refresh others. You were not filled only for yourself but to be a source of life to the world.
devotional.reflection: Who is being refreshed by the living water flowing through you?
devotional.prayer: Lord, let rivers of living water flow from me to refresh those around me. Amen.

verse.text: Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.

devotional.title: The Light of Life
devotional.body: Jesus is the light of the world, and those who follow Him will not walk in darkness. You do not need to see the whole path, only enough light for the next step. Keep following the light.
devotional.reflection: What step is the light of Jesus revealing for you to take today?
devotional.prayer: Jesus, You are my light. Lead me out of darkness and into life. Amen.

verse.text: And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.

devotional.title: The Truth Makes You Free
devotional.body: Jesus promised that knowing the truth brings freedom. Freedom comes when you know the reality of God's love and forgiveness. Lies keep you bound; truth breaks every chain.
devotional.reflection: What lie have you believed that the truth of God is ready to set you free from?
devotional.prayer: Lord, let Your truth reach every place where I am bound and set me free. Amen.

verse.text: If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.

devotional.title: Free Indeed
devotional.body: Jesus does not just promise freedom; He is the source of it. When the Son makes you free, you are truly free, free in a way no one else can give. Stop living as if you are still in chains.
devotional.reflection: Are you living like a person Jesus has truly set free?
devotional.prayer: Lord, thank You that You have made me free indeed. Help me live in that freedom. Amen.

verse.text: The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.

devotional.title: Abundant Life
devotional.body: Jesus came to give life, and not just any life but life in abundance. The thief works to steal and destroy; Jesus works to give. Your life with Him is meant to be full, not merely surviving.
devotional.reflection: What is stealing life from you that Jesus came to restore?
devotional.prayer: Lord, give me the abundant life You came to bring. Restore what has been stolen. Amen.

verse.text: I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.

devotional.title: The Good Shepherd
devotional.body: A hired hand runs when danger comes, but the good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep. Jesus proved His love on the cross. You are not cared for by a distant master but by a Shepherd who gave everything for you.
devotional.reflection: What does it mean to you that Jesus gave His life for you personally?
devotional.prayer: Good Shepherd, thank You for laying down Your life for me. Help me follow Your voice. Amen.

verse.text: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish.

devotional.title: His Sheep Hear His Voice
devotional.body: Jesus knows His sheep, and His sheep know His voice and follow Him. The Shepherd's voice is the one you can trust above all the noise. Learn to recognize it, and you will never be led astray.
devotional.reflection: How can you become more familiar with the voice of the Shepherd?
devotional.prayer: Lord, teach me to recognize Your voice and to follow You above every other sound. Amen.

verse.text: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live.

devotional.title: Resurrection and Life
devotional.body: Standing before a grave, Jesus declared that He Himself is the resurrection and the life. Death is not the final word for those who believe. Your hope is not in circumstances but in a person.
devotional.reflection: Where has death or loss made you forget that Jesus is the resurrection?
devotional.prayer: Jesus, You are the resurrection and the life. Anchor my hope in You. Amen.

verse.text: If any man serve me, let him follow me; and where I am, there shall also my servant be.

devotional.title: Serve Him
devotional.body: Jesus calls those who serve Him to follow Him and promises they will be where He is. Service and following are inseparable. Your service is not a detour; it is the path to being near Him.
devotional.reflection: Is your service flowing from following Jesus closely?
devotional.prayer: Lord, help me serve You by following You closely wherever You lead. Amen.

verse.text: A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you.

devotional.title: Love One Another
devotional.body: Jesus raised the bar of love: love one another as He loved you. His love was sacrificial, humble, and unconditional. This is the mark that identifies His followers.
devotional.reflection: Who is God calling you to love the way Jesus has loved you?
devotional.prayer: Lord, teach me to love others the way You have loved me. Amen.

verse.text: Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me.

devotional.title: Let Not Your Heart Be Troubled
devotional.body: Jesus spoke these words on the night He was betrayed, when everything seemed to be falling apart. He told His disciples to believe in Him as they believed in God. The answer to a troubled heart is trust.
devotional.reflection: What is troubling your heart that you need to bring to Jesus in trust?
devotional.prayer: Lord, my heart is troubled. I choose to believe in You. Give me Your peace. Amen.

verse.text: Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

devotional.title: The Way, the Truth, the Life
devotional.body: Jesus did not say He knows the way; He said He is the way. He is not just a teacher of truth but truth itself, not just a giver of life but life itself. Your access to the Father is through Him alone.
devotional.reflection: Are you looking for a way to God other than through Jesus?
devotional.prayer: Jesus, You are the way, the truth, and the life. I come to the Father through You. Amen.

verse.text: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.

devotional.title: My Peace I Give
devotional.body: The peace Jesus gives is not like the world's peace, which depends on circumstances. His peace remains when circumstances fall apart. Receive the peace He offers, and let it guard your heart.
devotional.reflection: Are you holding onto a peace that depends on circumstances or the peace of Christ?
devotional.prayer: Lord, give me Your peace, not the world's. Guard my heart from fear. Amen.

verse.text: I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.

devotional.title: Abide in the Vine
devotional.body: A branch does not strain to produce fruit; it simply abides in the vine, drawing life. Fruitfulness flows from connection, not effort. Abide in Christ, and fruit comes as a byproduct of your nearness.
devotional.reflection: Are you producing through striving or through abiding in Christ?
devotional.prayer: Lord, teach me to abide in You and let my life bear lasting fruit. Amen.

verse.text: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.

devotional.title: Lay Down Your Life
devotional.body: Jesus defined the greatest love: laying down one's life for friends. He did this literally on the cross. Loving at this level is sacrificial, giving of yourself for the good of another.
devotional.reflection: In what practical way can you lay down your life for someone today?
devotional.prayer: Lord, teach me the love that gives without counting the cost. Amen.

verse.text: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.

devotional.title: Overcome the World
devotional.body: Jesus was honest: you will have trouble in the world. But He also gave a reason for cheer: He has overcome the world. The outcome is already decided. You can face tribulation with peace because He has won.
devotional.reflection: What tribulation can you face with cheer because Jesus has already overcome?
devotional.prayer: Lord, thank You that You have overcome the world. Give me peace in the middle of trouble. Amen.

verse.text: Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.

devotional.title: Sanctified by Truth
devotional.body: Jesus prayed that His followers would be sanctified, set apart, through the truth of God's word. The Bible is the instrument God uses to make us holy. Let the truth reshape you.
devotional.reflection: How is God's truth currently setting you apart from the world?
devotional.prayer: Lord, sanctify me through Your truth. Let Your word shape who I am. Amen.

verse.text: Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.

devotional.title: Blessed Are Those Who Believe
devotional.body: Thomas believed because he saw, but Jesus blessed those who believe without seeing. You belong to that blessed company. Your faith, held without sight, is precious to Jesus.
devotional.reflection: What are you believing without seeing, and how is that faith blessed?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I believe even without seeing. Bless my faith and strengthen it. Amen.

verse.text: Jesus saith unto him, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me.

devotional.title: Follow Thou Me
devotional.body: Peter wanted to know about another disciple's future, but Jesus redirected him: what is that to you? Follow Me. Comparing your path to someone else's is a distraction. Your calling is simply to follow Jesus.
devotional.reflection: Who are you comparing yourself to instead of focusing on following Jesus?
devotional.prayer: Lord, help me focus on my own call to follow You and not on others' paths. Amen.

verse.text: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me.

devotional.title: Power From the Spirit
devotional.body: Jesus promised His followers power through the Holy Spirit to be His witnesses. Witnessing is not about your eloquence but His power. The Spirit equips you for what you cannot do alone.
devotional.reflection: Where are you relying on your own ability instead of the Spirit's power?
devotional.prayer: Lord, fill me with Your Spirit and make me a faithful witness wherever I go. Amen.

verse.text: Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.

devotional.title: No Other Name
devotional.body: Peter declared that salvation is found in no one but Jesus. The name of Jesus carries a power no other name can claim. In Him is the only way of salvation for all who call on Him.
devotional.reflection: Do you live with the confidence that salvation is secure in Jesus' name?
devotional.prayer: Lord, thank You for salvation in the name of Jesus, the only name that saves. Amen.

verse.text: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved.

devotional.title: Believe and Be Saved
devotional.body: The jailer asked what he must do to be saved, and the answer was simple: believe on the Lord Jesus Christ. Salvation is received through faith, not achieved through effort. Your part is to believe.
devotional.reflection: Have you placed your faith in Jesus, or are you still trying to save yourself?
devotional.prayer: Lord Jesus, I believe in You. Thank You for salvation that comes by faith. Amen.

verse.text: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.

devotional.title: Blessed to Give
devotional.body: Jesus taught that giving brings more blessing than receiving. It goes against our natural instincts, but generosity expands the heart. Try it: give something today, and discover the blessing.
devotional.reflection: What can you give today to experience the blessing of generosity?
devotional.prayer: Lord, help me to give freely and discover the blessing that comes from it. Amen.

verse.text: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.

devotional.title: I Believe God
devotional.body: In a storm at sea, Paul stood and declared that he believed God, and it would be just as he had been told. Faith anchors you in the storm. Believe what God has said, and let it settle your heart.
devotional.reflection: What has God told you that you need to believe in the middle of your storm?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I believe You. Let it be to me even as You have said. Amen.

verse.text: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth.

devotional.title: Not Ashamed
devotional.body: Paul was unashamed of the gospel because it is the power of God for salvation. It does not rely on human cleverness or polish; it carries the power of God. Never be embarrassed of the message that changes lives.
devotional.reflection: In what situation have you been tempted to be ashamed of the gospel?
devotional.prayer: Lord, give me boldness to be unashamed of the gospel that carries Your power. Amen.

verse.text: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

devotional.title: While We Were Yet Sinners
devotional.body: God did not wait for you to become good before loving you. While you were still a sinner, Christ died for you. His love is not earned or deserved; it is given. Let this love be your foundation.
devotional.reflection: How does knowing Christ died for you while you were still a sinner change your gratitude?
devotional.prayer: God, thank You for loving me before I was worthy. I receive Your love today. Amen.

verse.text: Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.

devotional.title: Peace With God
devotional.body: Through faith in Jesus, you are justified, declared righteous, and given peace with God. The war between you and your Maker is over. This peace is not something you produce; it is a gift you receive.
devotional.reflection: Are you living in the peace that Jesus purchased, or still trying to earn it?
devotional.prayer: Lord, thank You for peace with God through Jesus. Let that peace settle my heart. Amen.

verse.text: And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope.

devotional.title: Tribulation Works Patience
devotional.body: Paul describes a chain reaction: trouble produces endurance, endurance produces character, and character produces hope. Difficulties are not wasted when they are given to God. Let the trial do its good work in you.
devotional.reflection: What patience or character is God building in you through your current trial?
devotional.prayer: Lord, work patience, character, and hope in me through what I face. Amen.

verse.text: For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

devotional.title: The Gift of God
devotional.body: Sin pays a wage you do not want, but God gives a gift you could never earn. Eternal life is not a paycheck for good behavior; it is a gift received through Jesus. Receive it with open hands.
devotional.reflection: Are you trying to earn eternal life, or have you received it as a gift?
devotional.prayer: Lord, thank You for the gift of eternal life through Jesus Christ. I receive it. Amen.

verse.text: There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus.

devotional.title: No Condemnation
devotional.body: For those in Christ Jesus, there is no condemnation. The shame of the past does not have the final word. You can stop rehearsing your failures because Christ has paid for them.
devotional.reflection: What condemnation are you carrying that Jesus has already removed?
devotional.prayer: Lord, thank You that there is no condemnation for those in Christ. Help me live free. Amen.

verse.text: For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.

devotional.title: A Mind of Peace
devotional.body: Where you set your mind determines what you experience. A mind set on the flesh produces death, but a mind set on the Spirit produces life and peace. Choose today what your mind will dwell on.
devotional.reflection: What are you setting your mind on most, and what fruit is it producing?
devotional.prayer: Lord, set my mind on Your Spirit, that I may experience life and peace. Amen.

verse.text: For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father.

devotional.title: Abba, Father
devotional.body: You have not been given a spirit of fear but the Spirit of adoption. You can call God Father, with the intimacy of a child. Fear of rejection ends when you know you have been adopted into His family.
devotional.reflection: Where is fear keeping you from living as a confident child of God?
devotional.prayer: Father, thank You for adopting me. Help me live as Your child without fear. Amen.

verse.text: What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who can be against us?

devotional.title: God Is for Us
devotional.body: Paul's question is meant to end all fear: if God is for you, who can be against you? No force in heaven or earth can outweigh the God who stands on your side. Your odds have changed.
devotional.reflection: What opposition seems large that is smaller than the God who is for you?
devotional.prayer: Lord, if You are for me, who can be against me? Strengthen my confidence in You. Amen.

verse.text: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

devotional.title: Nothing Can Separate
devotional.body: Paul lists everything that might try to separate you from God's love and declares them all powerless. Not death, not circumstances, not spiritual powers. Nothing in all creation can separate you from His love.
devotional.reflection: What are you afraid might separate you from God's love?
devotional.prayer: Lord, nothing can separate me from Your love. Let me rest in that unshakable truth. Amen.

verse.text: That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.

devotional.title: Confess and Believe
devotional.body: Salvation involves both the mouth and the heart: confessing Jesus as Lord and believing in His resurrection. This is not a formula for perfection but a doorway to new life. The door is open to you.
devotional.reflection: Have you made this confession of faith your own?
devotional.prayer: Lord Jesus, I confess You as Lord and believe God raised You from the dead. Save me. Amen.

verse.text: For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.

devotional.title: Whosoever Calls
devotional.body: The invitation is universal: whosoever calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. There is no fine print, no limit on who may call. Whatever your background, the door is open.
devotional.reflection: Are you calling on the Lord, or waiting until you feel worthy enough?
devotional.prayer: Lord, I call upon Your name. Thank You for saving whosoever calls. Amen.

verse.text: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

devotional.title: Transformed Minds
devotional.body: The world pressures you into its mold, but God calls you to transformation through a renewed mind. Change begins in the way you think. Renew your mind in God's truth and your life will follow.
devotional.reflection: What thought patterns need to be renewed to match God's will?
devotional.prayer: Lord, renew my mind and transform me. Help me prove Your good and perfect will. Amen.

verse.text: Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.

devotional.title: Overcome Evil With Good
devotional.body: Evil often invites you to respond in kind, but that is how it wins. The call is higher: overcome evil with good. Your response to wrong can be the beginning of redemption.
devotional.reflection: Where are you tempted to return evil, and what good could overcome it?
devotional.prayer: Lord, give me the strength to overcome evil with good in every situation. Amen.

verse.text: Love worketh no ill to his neighbour: therefore love is the fulfilling of the law.

devotional.title: Love Fulfills the Law
devotional.body: Love does no harm to a neighbor, and love is the fulfilling of the law. Rules are simplified when love is the motivation. Let love be the guide that keeps you on the right path.
devotional.reflection: How would your obedience change if love, not duty, was your motive?
devotional.prayer: Lord, let love be the fulfillment of everything You ask of me. Amen.

verse.text: Let us therefore follow after the things which make for peace, and things wherewith one may edify another.

devotional.title: Make for Peace
devotional.body: Paul urges believers to pursue peace and to build one another up. Peace is not always easy, and building others up takes intentionality. Make it your aim today.
devotional.reflection: What would pursuing peace and building up others look like in your relationships?
devotional.prayer: Lord, help me follow after peace and use my words to build others up. Amen.

verse.text: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.

devotional.title: The God of Hope
devotional.body: Paul prays that the God of hope would fill you with joy and peace as you believe, so you abound in hope. Joy, peace, and hope are not feelings you manufacture; they come from God as you trust Him.
devotional.reflection: Where do you need the God of hope to fill you with joy and peace?
devotional.prayer: God of hope, fill me with all joy and peace as I believe in You. Amen.

verse.text: But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty.

devotional.title: God Chooses the Foolish
devotional.body: God often works through what the world considers foolish and weak to reveal His power. Do not discount your weakness; it may be exactly where God chooses to work. Your limitations showcase His strength.
devotional.reflection: What weakness has God used or could use to display His power?
devotional.prayer: Lord, use the foolish and weak things in my life to confound the wise. Amen.

verse.text: But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him.

devotional.title: Prepared for Those Who Love Him
devotional.body: God has prepared things for those who love Him that exceed anything you can imagine or have heard. Your best days are not behind you. What God has prepared is greater than you can conceive.
devotional.reflection: How does the promise of unseen blessings give you hope for the future?
devotional.prayer: Lord, thank You for what You have prepared for those who love You. I trust Your future for me. Amen.

verse.text: For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.

devotional.title: One Foundation
